title: Embedded JSON parsing bypasses configured nesting-depth validation
reasoning: The pure-JSON path calls _safe_json_loads, which validates max_json_nesting_depth after json.loads. The embedded path decodes objects with JSONDecoder.raw_decode and immediately extracts tool calls without calling _validate_json_depth. That creates inconsistent trust-boundary enforcement: a deeply nested tool-call args payload is rejected when it is the whole response but can be accepted when wrapped in surrounding text.
reproduction: Set a low max_json_nesting_depth and parse an embedded response containing `prefix {"functionCall":{"name":"read_file","args":{"a":{"b":{"c":1}}}}} suffix`. The embedded raw_decode path reaches schema extraction and validation without the depth check used by _safe_json_loads.
recommendation: Run _validate_json_depth(parsed, self.limits.max_json_nesting_depth) after raw_decode and before schema extraction in parse_embedded_json, converting RecursionError to ParseValidationError consistently with _safe_json_loads.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise timeout, extraction, removal, max_response_size, max_json_size for trailing text, and validator constraints, but none assert that embedded JSON observes max_json_nesting_depth.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parser_extraction test that configures max_json_nesting_depth to a small value and asserts an embedded over-depth functionCall raises ParseValidationError.
minimumFixScope: Add depth validation to the embedded JSON path and focused regression coverage.
